problem:
Let $V=C[0,1],$ the vector space of functions that are continuous over $[0,1].$ Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t,
$$

find the orthogonal projection of $f(t)=12({t}^{2}-t)$ onto the subspace spanned by $g(t)=t-1.$

activity_context.topic_title: Projecting Vectors Onto Subspaces in Inner Product Spaces

feedback.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1],$ the vector space of functions that are continuous over $[0,1].$ Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t,
$$

find the orthogonal projection of $f(t)=4{t}^{2}$ onto the subspace spanned by $g(t)=6t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $f(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{g(t)}$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{g(t)}\,f(t)=\frac{⟨f(t),g(t)⟩}{⟨g(t),g(t)⟩}\,g(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),g(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{t}^{2}\cdot 6t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}24{t}^{3}\,\text{d}t \\  & =[6{t}^{4}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =6-0 \\  & =6,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨g(t),g(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(6t)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}36{t}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & =[12{t}^{3}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =12-0 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the projection is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{g(t)}\,f(t) & =\frac{⟨f(t),g(t)⟩}{⟨g(t),g(t)⟩}\,g(t) \\  & =\frac{6}{12}\cdot 6t \\  & =3t.\end{aligned}
$$
